context: I Theorem 3. No probabilistic algorithm can produce with positive probability a sequence ω that is α-everywhere complex for some α ∈ (0, 1). P∞ I Theorem 4. Let i=0 ai be a computable converging series of nonnegative rational numbers. There exists a probabilistic algorithm that produces with probability 1 some sequence ω such that K(ω([k, k + n))) ≥ a[log n] n − c for some c and for all k and n. I Theorem 5. No probabilistic algorithm can produce with positive probability a sequence ω with the following property: there exists a non-decreasing unbounded computable function g : N → N such that K(ω([k, k + n)) | k, n) ≥ g(n) for all k and n. Theorem 3 and 4 complement each other: the first one says that α-everywhere complex sequences for a fixed α > 0 (even very small) cannot be obtained by a probabilistic algorithm; √ the second one says that if we allow sublinear growth and replace the bound αn by n or 2 n/ log n, then the probabilistic algorithm exists. (There are intermediate cases where none of these theorems is applicable, say, n/ log n bound; we do not know the answer for these cases.) Theorem 5 says that Theorem 4 cannot be extended to the case of the generalized Levin lemma; here the answer is negative for any computable non-decreasing unbounded function. 3 Proof of Theorem 4 Let us start with the positive result.
